title: Aging and Late Adulthood
summary: Aging: physical, cognitive and social-emotional changes in late adulthood; theories of ageing; issues in late adulthood (retirement, bereavement, wisdom).
revision: Aging and late adulthood: physical, cognitive, social-emotional changes; ageing theories; integrity vs despair.

notes.t: The period from age 65 to death, the final stage of the lifespan.

i: Physical: sensory decline, slower processing, health changes
Cognitive: crystallised intelligence stable, fluid intelligence may decline
Social-emotional: retirement, bereavement, wisdom, life review
Activity theory: staying active promotes successful ageing
Disengagement theory: mutual withdrawal is natural and acceptable
Continuity theory: maintain familiar patterns and roles

notes.t: Erikson's final stage: life review produces wisdom (integrity) or regret (despair).
UGC NET frequently asks about ageing theories and Erikson's final stage.

mnemonics.title: ACDC
mnemonics.text: A — Activity theory (stay active), C — Continuity theory (maintain patterns), D — Disengagement theory (mutual withdrawal), C — Crystallised vs fluid intelligence
